Population of legislative districts by Region, Province, and selected Highly Urbanized/Component City : 2015 |publisher=[[Philippine Statistics Authority]] |accessdate=February 23, 2021 |archive-date=April 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220405172113/http://rsso03.psa.gov.ph/sites/default/files/Philippines%20-%20Population%20of%20Legislative%20Districts%20by%20Region_Province_and%20Selected%20Highly%20Urbanized%20or%20Component%20City.xlsx |url-status=dead }} |electorate = 337,583 (2022){{cite web|url=https://comelec.gov.ph/?r=2022NLE/Statistics/2022RVVAVmcocfinal|title=Number and Turn-Out of Registered Voters and Voters Who Actually Voted by City/Municipality May 9, 2022 National and Local Elections|website=Commission on Elections|accessdate=June 30, 2023}} |area = {{convert|2395.64|sqkm|sqmi|abbr=on}} |towns = {{Collapsible list | titlestyle = font-weight:normal;text-align:left;background-color:WhiteSmoke; | title = 6 [[Local government in the Philippines|LGU]]s | '''Cities''' | [[Tagum]] | '''Municipalities''' | [[Asuncion, Davao del Norte|Asuncion]] | [[Kapalong]] | [[New Corella]] | [[San Isidro, Davao del Norte|San Isidro]] | [[Talaingod]] }} |year = 1987 |members_label = Representative |members = Oyo Uy |blank1_name = Political party |blank1_info = {{Color box|{{party color|Lakas–CMD}}|border=darkgray}} [[Lakas–CMD|Lakas]] |blank2_name = Congressional bloc |blank2_info = Majority }} '''Davao del Norte's 1st congressional district''' is one of the two [[congressional districts of the Philippines]] in the province of [[Davao del Norte]]. It has been represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] since 1987.{{cite web |url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |title=Roster of Philippine legislators |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=February 23, 2021 |archive-date=March 16, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170316064243/http://congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |url-status=dead }} The district covers the northern and eastern parts of the province including its capital, [[Tagum]], and the municipalities of [[Asuncion, Davao del Norte|Asuncion]], [[Kapalong]], [[New Corella]], [[San Isidro, Davao del Norte|San Isidro]] and [[Talaingod]].{{cite web |url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/1998/01/30/republic-act-no-8470/ |title=Republic Act No. 8740 |date=30 January 1998 |publisher=[[Official Gazette (Philippines)]] |accessdate=February 23, 2021 |archive-date=1 December 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201041924/http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/1998/01/30/republic-act-no-8470/ |url-status=dead }}{{cite web|url=https://www.chanrobles.com/ordinance.htm |title=The 1987 Constitution of the Republic of the Philippines |publisher=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library |accessdate=February 23, 2021}} It is currently represented in the [[20th Congress of the Philippines|20th Congress]] by Oyo Uy of the [[Lakas–CMD]] (Lakas).{{cite web|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/members/ |title=House Members |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=February 23, 2021}} From 1987 to 1998, the district covered the eastern municipalities of [[Compostela, Davao de Oro|Compostela]], [[Maragusan]], [[Mawab]], [[Monkayo]], [[Montevista, Davao de Oro|Montevista]], [[Nabunturan]], and [[New Bataan]]. These municipalities comprised much of the Compostela Valley and were separated from Davao del Norte to form the present-day province of [[Davao de Oro]] in 1998.{{cite PH act |url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/1998/01/30/republic-act-no-8470/ |title=An Act Creating the Province of Compostela , Valley From the Province of Davao Del Norte, and for Other Purposes|chamber=RA|number=8740 |date=30 January 1998 |publisher=[[Official Gazette (Philippines)]] |accessdate=February 24, 2021 |archive-date=1 December 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201041924/http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/1998/01/30/republic-act-no-8470/ |url-status=dead }} ==Representation history== {| class=wikitable |- ! rowspan="2" | # ! rowspan="2" colspan=2 | Image ! rowspan="2" | Member ! colspan=2 | Term of office ! rowspan="2" | Congress ! rowspan="2" | Party ! rowspan="2" | Electoral history ! rowspan="2" | Constituent
